Hi Claire — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the MAAP. Below is a concise pricing/options matrix and the team’s starting position so we can move quickly:

Option A — Pilot (6 months) with amortized platform fee
- Operator license: $18,000/site/year (covers licensing for the serving runtime).
- Platform fee: $36,000 (annual list). For pilot we can amortize this over 12 months (apply 50% of one year as upfront charge) = $18,000 due at kickoff, remainder billed monthly.
- Support: Standard (8x5) included; Premium (24x7 + 2 incidents/year SLO guarantee) add $10k/month.
- SRE retainer (optional): Bronze $7k/mo, Silver $15k/mo, Gold $28k/mo (onsite travel billed separately).
- Hardware escrow: we treat escrow for OSS drivers/artifacts as an addendum; recommended approach is a one‑time escrow setup fee of $6,500 + annual verification fee $2,000. Escrow can be invoiced to Medisys or held on Redwood’s custodial agreement depending on Legal’s preference.

Option B — Pilot with larger upfront credit (conversion incentive)
- If Medisys commits to a 24‑month conversion at pilot kickoff, Redwood will provide a one‑time migration credit equal to 25% of the platform fee at conversion. This can cover escrow setup or be applied against the first quarter of Premium support.

Notes / tradeoffs:
- We can cap upfront cash for pilot by moving 50% of platform fee into monthly billing and placing the remainder on a conversion credit memo tied to a PO.
- Operator license is per active deployment site; burst nodes are billed separately by node class.
- Any escrow/legal redlines that expand indemnity will require finance review and may affect the credit sizing.

I’ve attached a pricing workbook that lays these scenarios side‑by‑side and a sample SOW template. If these options look reasonable I can hand off to Marissa for a formal redline and to Naomi for commercial approval.

Best,
Dylan

- I recommend we accept the 50% amortization for the platform fee for the pilot (keeps their Opex low) but require a signed PO that triggers the first amortized payment.
- Approve the 25% conversion credit but cap its application to platform fee or SRE retainer only (no refunds against past invoice line items).

- If procurement is pushing for a larger discount on platform fee, counter with an operational commitment (e.g., a 12‑month minimum at conversion).

I’ll draft a compact commercial amendment we can send with the MAAP. Naomi — can you confirm the margin floor if we give 25% conversion credit + 10% off platform fee?

1) Platform fee: Medisys requests a 30% discount on the annual platform fee for the pilot period if Redwood will commit to the 12‑month amortization structure you outlined.
2) Conversion credit: we accept the 25% conversion credit but ask that it be executable within 60 days of GA if conversion is signalled.
